deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page is a draft of the topological preliminaries (Analysis-situs section) of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). The previous page proves the following. Suppose a surface T is cut by n Querschnitte into m simply connected pieces. Then n − m is the same for every such decomposition. A Querschnitt is a cut running from a boundary point to a boundary point.

This page names that invariant and records how it behaves under different kinds of cuts.

(1) Definition. The deleted opening was roughly 'Durch die Zerschneidung einer ...'. The surviving text reads: 'Wir nennen diese constante Zahl [n − m] die Ordnung des Zusammenhangs der Fläche T.' An interlinear phrase, probably 'um 1 kleiner', tries to tie this 'Ordnung' to the usual 'k-fach zusammenhängend' count. Compare the previous page: a connected piece that becomes simply connected after μ+1 cuts is called (μ+2)-fach zusammenhängend, and it has n − m = (μ+1) − 1 = μ.

In modern terms (my gloss), take a compact surface with boundary and components T_i. Each component needs b1(T_i) cuts to become simply connected. So n − m = Σ(b1(T_i) − 1) = b1 − b0 = −χ(T). Riemann's 'Ordnung des Zusammenhangs' here is the negative Euler characteristic. Read this way it is defined for disconnected surfaces and is additive over pieces, which is exactly how the page uses it.

(2) Behaviour under cuts. 'Ordnung des Zusammenhangs ... der Stücke, in welche sie zerfällt' means the invariant is computed for the cut surface, summed over its pieces. Riemann then states three rules (my verification in brackets):
(a) Every Querschnitt (boundary to boundary) lowers the order by 1. [Cutting along a properly embedded arc raises χ by 1, so −χ drops by 1. This holds whether or not the cut disconnects the surface. It also follows directly from the invariance of n − m: a Querschnitt Q followed by a decomposition of the cut surface with n', m' gives a decomposition of T with n'+1 cuts and the same m'.]
(b) A cut running from one interior point to another interior point (a slit) raises the order by 1. [Removing an interior arc is homotopy-equivalent to removing a point, so χ decreases by 1. Equivalently, the slit becomes a new boundary component.]
(c) A cut running back into itself in the interior (a closed curve) leaves the order unchanged. [χ(S¹) = 0, so χ is unchanged whether or not the curve separates.]

The first version of (c) was struck out on line 5–6 and rewritten on lines 8–9 after (b) was inserted.
errors: No mathematical errors. Statements (a), (b), (c) are all correct for n − m = −χ.

The interlinear relation between 'Ordnung' and the 'fach' count (probably 'um 1 kleiner') is too faint to verify. For a connected surface the previous page implies 'fach' = Ordnung + 2, not +1, so the interlinear wording may refer to something else, e.g. the number of cuts. This is unresolved.
Implicit assumption, not stated: (b) and (c) require the cut to lie in the interior and not meet existing boundary or earlier cuts.

results.what: Definition of the order of connectivity as the decomposition invariant n − m (cuts minus simply connected pieces); this equals −χ
results.modern_name: Order of connectivity / negative Euler characteristic (first Betti number minus number of components)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen); Euler characteristic of surfaces later systematized by Möbius, Jordan, Betti

results.what: A Querschnitt lowers the order of connectivity by exactly 1
results.modern_name: Effect of cutting along a properly embedded arc on χ

results.what: An interior slit (point to point) raises the order by 1; a closed interior cut leaves it unchanged
results.modern_name: Additivity/excision behaviour of the Euler characteristic (χ(arc)=1, χ(S¹)=0)
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Riemann 1857 and later combinatorial topology (Jordan 1866, etc.)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known topological section of Riemann's 1857 Abelian functions paper. The explicit rules for interior slits and closed interior cuts are a small unpublished detail, but they are elementary consequences of the published theory.

checkable.asserts: A connected genus-g surface with b>=1 boundary circles needs n=2g+b-1 Querschnitte to become one simply connected piece (m=1). Hence n-m = -χ = 2g+b-2 (difference = 0).
A disc with k holes has n-m = k-1 = -χ (difference = 0).
A Querschnitt raises χ by 1, so the order -χ drops by 1 (difference = 0).
An interior slit lowers χ by 1, so the order rises by 1 (difference = 0).

Line 2: 'die Ordnung des Zusammenhangs der Fläche T.' (the letter T is visible), followed by an interlinear '; die Ordnung'.
Lines 5–6: the struck passage is '[und durch einen ... im Innern in sich zurücklaufenden Schnitt nicht verändert]'; it was moved to lines 8–9.
